RECALL
During the development of the All-Bank Tech strategy, Technology leadership aligned on consolidating the activities and teams focused on end-user experience and enablement under a single mandate within the GTEP organization. The consolidation commenced in January 2026 with the hiring of Peter Capraro as the VP, Global Employee Digital Experience. Under Peter, WXE’s mandate is to deliver on Initiative C8 (Develop and Implement an Integrated Strategy for All End User Services to Create a Simplified Workplace Experience that Enables Employee Productivity) within the All-Bank Tech Strategy and to support GTEP’s focus on creating Exceptional Colleague Experiences.
KEY POINTS
Context and Current State:
Context: WXE is BNS’ first globally integrated team responsible for engineering and designing workplaces and optimizing colleague productivity and experience. The team designs, engineers, and manages global workplace experiences aimed at elevating our colleagues' productivity, strengthening the Bank’s resilience, and maintaining cost discipline. We aim to deliver this mandate through an integrated operating model (WIP) that elevates engineering rigor and product mgmt philosophy, supported by an intelligence layer (DEX) (see slide 3)
Current State and Case for change: Today, BNS’ endpoint estate does not meet modern requirements and is eroding our colleague's productivity while increasing risk exposure and capital costs. The estate supports ~90k employees with predominantly physical and windows devices (~130K physical devices and ~8K virtual, ~6% virtual), with a relatively high device ratio (1.27). BNS has historically not managed the experience, demand, or cost of the endpoint estate in a centralized mandate, creating a substantial need/opportunity to manage risk and lower capital costs (see slide 4). At the same time, the current estate further amplifies BNS’ exposure to volatile hardware market prices and evolving security threats; meanwhile, peers lead BNS with more virtual, diversified, and dynamically managed estates (see slide 5).
Path Forward:  In response, WXE has defined a go forward mission and 6 strategic priorities aligned to the GTEP and All-Bank Technology Strategy: Deliver a seamless provisioning experience; Curate exceptional colleague offerings; Globalize &  modernize support operations; Enable intelligence & proactive response; Establish a global workplace hardware estate; Win as a global unified team (see slide 6). 
Vision: WXE has developed a clear perspective of what the future of WXE should look and feel like by the end of F28: combining a zero-touch provisioning experience with curated & persona-based workplace offerings and a proactive and globally standardized support operation, which is centrally managed through a DEX intelligence layer (see slide 7). 
Critical Work: We have identified a portfolio of 35 critical work initiatives across our 6 strategic priorities to deliver on WXE’s mandate (see slide 8)
Mobilization: WXE’s leadership team is actively working on defining and orchestrating the detailed milestone roadmap of when and how value will be unlocked for BNS (see slide 9).
Deep Dive - End-User Strategy: The new end-user strategy will shift BNS away from a device-centric model to a segmented, hybrid endpoint strategy driven by DEX. The focus of this work will be to optimize device diversity, introducing a clear persona-based segmentation of our workforce, and building/integrating the critical DEX intelligence layer. (see slide 12)
Optimizing Device Diversity: The new diversified endpoint portfolio (Mac, Cloud PC, Enterprise browser) de-risks the estate and introduces true workspace continuity. (see slide 13)
Introducing Segmentation: Personas will involve distinct physical, virtual, and mobile endpoint postures to better optimize colleague experience, risk, and cost. Specifically, we will deliver fundamentally different workspaces based on the personas' mobility, consistency, and performance needs. (see slide 14 & 15)
Building the Intelligence Layer: It is critical we integrate a DEX system that makes the end‑user strategy observable, controllable, and scalable (see slide 16)
Mobilization: We will be delivering the modern workplace across the Enterprise in phased approaches with key pilots delivered in the U.S. over the next ~3 quarters (see slide 17)
NEXT STEPS
The WXE leadership team is currently articulating the measures of success and detailed strategy roadmap to define the timing of critical milestones (~tentatively wrapped up by early June)

Mexico operates in a stable macroeconomic environment, supported by solid fundamentals, a large and young workforce, and deep North American integration. While near‑term growth is expected to remain moderate, the environment remains constructive for disciplined, profitable banking growth
SBM is at a pivotal moment. The franchise is delivering on the 2026 plan, anchored in a strong Risk and Control operation. At the same time, SBM is yet to reach its full potential, and acceleration in client acquisition and share-of-wallet growth 
While Q1 FY26 results exceed plan across key metrics reflecting early traction, structural factors such as deposit and loan mix, client experience, and scale in priority segments persist as long-term challenges
Reaching the 2030 ambition will require more than momentum. It will depend on disciplined execution and targeted strategic choices to strengthen primacy, transactional volume and sustainable scale, with a sharper focus on distribution capabilities to strengthen our position

Robust governance and disciplined execution across strategic priorities, anchored by a strong, talented team
PCLs are stabilizing and exhibiting a positive trend; however, challenges persist with legacy portfolios
Wealth Management sustains momentum with double‑digit growth
Strong Corporate Banking franchise 
Commercial Banking on the right path to reach profitability

A deposit mix skewed toward higher cost of funds relative to peers
Excess concentration in secured lending leading to lower return in Retail Banking
Insufficient digital capabilities have driven a heavy reliance on branch execution while frontline sales productivity remains constrained
Under‑penetration of transactional banking solutions across segments challenging primacy
Accelerate penetration rates in GBM clients with focus on Cash Management and FX
Limited client acquisition and an uncompetitive payroll proposition have capped our scaling potential

Credit cards are central to everyday payments across LATAM (~65% cards penetration) and the Caribbean (~$305Bn credit card market volume), with high penetration, strong consumer preference, and a large, growing transaction base.

CONTEXT AND OBJECTIVES
Wealthsimple’s (“WS”) recent product announcements have garnered interest and attention across FIs and consumers on its offerings and value proposition
Given the attention, this fact-base was developed with the objectives to: 1) outline WS’s growth and impact on BNS; 2) understand their relative strengths, and 3) frame next steps and discuss if a further strategic response is required
WEALTHSIMPLE GROWTH STORY
Since its inception, WS has experienced strong growth; it now has ~3MM clients and has seen ~70% CAGR in assets since 2018 (vs. 8% for BNS and 4% for TNG) 
While outflows to WS across Retail, iTRADE and TNG account for 2% of total, net outflows to WS have grown by ~100% Y/Y and are overindexed from primary clients (~50% of outflows) 
Clients sending funds to WS skew younger and less affluent (e.g., clients aged 18–34 make up ~70% of WS outflow activity, despite representing only ~35% of our total client base)
WS leads the market in net switching-gains across most banking and investing products; BNS leads in GIC net-switching gains, and TNG is top three in chequing accts and RRSPs
Continued net outflows to WS could reduce our assets by $60-230Bn in next five years (~$0.2-1.2Bn impact on F30 run-rate revenue) and our primary clients by 5-20% of today’s base 
WEALTHSIMPLE STRENGTHS
Through primary and secondary research, Wealthsimple’s strengths have been identified along the following dimensions: 
Products: WS has strong direct investing and retail investing offerings (e.g., robo); WS continues to evolve its offering to meet client needs (e.g., banking) 
Pricing: WS offers value for money in the form of low cost, high rates; additionally, WS offers incentives and promotions with high rewards 
Experience: WS has created strong brand equity among its clients through its digital capabilities, branding, and two-way client engagement 
Enablers: WS’s ability to execute at pace can be attributed to their modern tech stack, agile delivery, calculated risk-taking culture, and long-term profitability horizon
PATH FORWARD
Near-term, WS will likely deepen its wealth and banking offerings; Medium-to-long-term, IPO is the likely destination for WS, allowing Power Corp. to unlock value from its stake
Across BNS and Tangerine, there are several strategies and investments in-flight that are expected to combat outflows to WS (e.g., Retail segmentation, iTRADE growth strategy, Project Clarity); time and resources are required to execute on these initiatives and realize benefits
Specifically, the highest priority initiatives to compete are:  
Tangerine ‘Project Clarity’ strategy, including the crypto offering
CX initiatives within CB and Wealth, particularly the digital experience
At this time, these initiatives are moving as quickly as possible; no further action is needed but we will continue to monitor progress

elements.text:
The Bank has an established Strategic Risk Management Framework (SRMF) that integrates inter-related enterprise-wide processes to manage and oversee strategic risk. 
The SRMF requires the First Line to ensure regulatory capital consumption and growth in Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) is supported by adequate revenue and profit generation. 
The Bank’s Strategic Planning incorporates Capital and Financial planning including key capital metrics and constraints. Global Risk Management (GRM) Senior Management, challenges the Bank’s Business Strategies and Plans considering the Bank’s strategic and financial priorities, and established Risk Appetite Metrics. 
GRM monitors the Bank’s execution of its strategy, horizon scan of emerging threats, and business environment via the Top & Emerging Risk Assessment process. This enables the development of an independent second line view of the Bank’s Strategic Risk Profile. 
GRM monitors the following risk metrics to oversee the Business’ capital consumption and revenue/profit generation as part of its monitoring activities: 
RoE, RoRWA, RAM (Enterprise Risk Appetite Metrics)1
Strategic KPIs (KPIs pertaining to the four pillars of the Bank’s strategy)
NIAT and PTPP v/s Plan2 
RoRWA and RWA growth v/s Plan
The Bank’s Strategic Risk Profile is reported to the Bank’s Risk Management Committee (RMC) and the Risk Committee of the Board on a quarterly basis via the Quarterly Risk Report (QRR).
